name: Particle physics: helical hit association with missing hits and clutter
description: Develop a particle-track reconstruction algorithm that associates noisy detector hits into charged-particle trajectories. This CPU-sized synthetic adaptation keeps curved trajectories, missing layers, unrelated hits and increasing occupancy from the TrackML problem setting. The candidate returns track memberships, and an independent evaluator computes signal-hit pair precision, recall and F1. Improvements can come from helix parameterization, Hough voting, sequential fitting, robust rejection or constrained global association.

sources.locator: The Tracking Machine Learning challenge: Accuracy phase; sections 1, 2.1-2.4 describe trajectory association, hit geometry, data and the official scoring problem.
CERN Document Server: TrackML: a tracking Machine Learning challenge; primary CERN-hosted description of the challenge.

limitations: Reduced synthetic adaptation, not an official CERN or TrackML benchmark; no official data or scores are reproduced.
Uniform idealized field, eight cylindrical layers and fewer than one thousand hits per event; no material interactions, endcaps, pileup collision model or calibrated detector units.
Pair F1 is a local objective and differs from the published weighted majority-match TrackML score; published leaderboard values are not comparable.
Four fixed public seeds support repeatable development, not a secret test set; independent fresh seeds are needed to assess generalization.

name: Particle physics: background-aware collider anomaly ranking
description: Improve an unsupervised anomaly ranker given a reference background sample and an unlabeled mixture containing localized anomalous overdensities. Inspired by the LHC Olympics collider-search setting, this reduced synthetic task uses nonlinear correlated five-dimensional features and six injected signal modes. Independent evaluation combines tie-aware AUROC with signal efficiency at a conservative 5% background acceptance. Explore covariance models, conditional densities, nearest-neighbor estimators or reference-to-mixture density ratios.

sources.locator: The LHC Olympics 2020: A Community Challenge for Anomaly Detection in High Energy Physics; section 2 (challenge), section 3.2.2 and figure 9 (ROC and signal/background efficiencies).
CERN EP newsletter, LHC Olympics 2020 Challenge: reference background, predominantly background black boxes, and localized overdensity searches.

limitations: Reduced synthetic adaptation, not an official LHC Olympics or CERN benchmark; no events, pretrained models or numerical published results are reused.
Five dimensionless illustrative features are not calibrated jet observables and are not a realistic Standard Model event simulation.

The local equal-weight AUROC/efficiency score is not an official competition ranking or calibrated discovery significance; the injected signal fraction is much larger than typical rare-signal searches.

The evaluator uses truth to choose a diagnostic efficiency threshold. The candidate does not provide a calibrated false-alarm probability, and a better score does not demonstrate new physics or solve dark matter.
Reference and evaluation samples are disjoint, but all six seeds and signal modes are public. Generalization requires fresh independent samples.
